16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔ READ THE DISK NUMBER BEFORE YOU SIZE THIS, NOT AFTER. Audiobookshelf stores the media itself on the VM, and audiobooks are large. The flavor disk is the entire budget: m1.small is 20 GB, m1.medium is 40 GB, m1.large is 80 GB. That is the WHOLE disk, before Ubuntu, dockerd, the image, /metadata covers and caches, and the app's own backups. On a different redu deployment (425, a Nextcloud install) an m1.medium reported 32.4 GB free of its 40 GB once the OS and the app were on it; that is a measurement of a different app and only a rough guide here, but the shape is right, so plan on roughly THREE QUARTERS of the flavor disk being usable for media. BE HONEST WITH THE USER BEFORE DEPLOYING: a large audiobook library does NOT fit on any flavor in this catalogue. Ask them how many gigabytes their library is. If the answer is more than about 30 GB, m1.medium is the wrong shape and they need either m1.large (80 GB, GBP 0.0486/hr, and NOT trial eligible) or an attached volume, per the next quirk."
18	  - "GROWING THE STORAGE IS A VOLUME OPERATION, NOT A REDEPLOY, SO DECIDE IT UP FRONT. redu block storage is a separate resource: create_volume (name, size in GB) then attach_volume (volume_id, instance_id). ⚠️ Attaching does NOT mount it: the instance keeps booting from its own root disk and the volume turns up as an extra block device, so you then need get_ssh_command, lsblk to find it (usually /dev/vdb), a filesystem on it, a mount, an /etc/fstab line, and the compose bind mount for /audiobooks pointed at the mount path. That is a real piece of work to retrofit onto a running library. This file has NO measured per-GB rate for volumes, so do not quote one: get the current price from the platform and put it in front of the user before creating anything."
19	  - "⛔ PIN FROM THE REGISTRY, AND NOTE THE TAG HAS NO LEADING v. The GitHub release is v2.36.0; the ghcr.io tag is ghcr.io/advplyr/audiobookshelf:2.36.0. Copying the release name gives you a tag that does not exist and a pull that fails. Verified against the anonymous ghcr.io tag list on 2026-08-17. Upstream's own example compose says :latest; never put that in a recipe, because a redeploy then silently crosses releases."
20	  - "⛔⛔ WHOEVER LOADS THE URL FIRST BECOMES ROOT, AND THEY CAN DO IT WITH NO PASSWORD. Verified at Server.js:343-349: POST /init has no authentication and is refused only once a root user already exists. Server.js:433-441: if the request body carries an EMPTY password, the root user is created WITHOUT one and the server merely logs a warning. LocalAuthStrategy.js:65-76 and :134 then permit that account to log in from anywhere with an empty password. So the failure mode is not just losing the instance, it is losing it to a caller who never had to choose a credential. There is no install wizard, no deploy-time admin variable, and no bootstrap token: «REDACTED:assigned:c462e8fc» closes this window except claiming the account. CLAIM IT AS PART OF THE DEPLOY, with a real password, before you hand the URL to anyone, and use the claim script in the body of this file so the claim is verified rather than assumed."
21	  - "✅ THE GOOD NEWS: THERE IS NO SELF-SIGNUP AT ALL, SO THE WINDOW CLOSES PERMANENTLY ONCE ROOT EXISTS. Verified: Auth.js:318-478 registers only /login, /logout, /auth/refresh and the OpenID routes, and ApiRouter.js:133 puts POST /api/users behind the admin middleware. There is no registration form and no setting to turn off, because the feature does not exist. After the root account is claimed, the only way anybody else gets an account is an admin creating one in Settings. Say this to the user plainly: it is the reason this app is safe on a public hostname once the first minute is dealt with."
22	  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The auth middleware is mounted on /api only (Server.js:320), and Auth.js:21,36-37 exempts two GETs even there. So without signing in, anyone can reach: GET /status (server version, and the CONFIG_PATH and METADATA_PATH of the host while uninitialised), GET /ping, GET /healthcheck, GET /api/items/<id>/cover, GET /api/authors/<id>/image, plus /feed/... RSS and /public/share/... which are opt-in per item and serve nothing until a user shares something. Cover art for a known item id is readable by anyone; the audio is not. None of that is alarming, but it is the honest answer, and /status is what the checks in this file gate on."
23	  - "⛔ DO NOT PROVISION A MANAGED DATABASE FOR THIS APP. It cannot use one. Database.js:232-234 hardcodes dialect sqlite with the file at /config/absdatabase.sqlite, and no other dialect appears anywhere in the file. Passing database:'managed' to deploy_compose would provision a Postgres VM that Audiobookshelf never opens a socket to, and bill for it forever. Leave deploy_compose's database parameter at its default ('compose'); the stack has no db service, so nothing extra is created. This also means the usual library warning is inverted here: there is no silent SQLite fallback to detect, because SQLite is the design."
24	  - "⛔ THEREFORE THE /config VOLUME IS THE DATABASE. Everything that is not a media file lives in /config/absdatabase.sqlite: accounts, permissions, listening progress, sessions, API keys, library definitions and the JWT signing secret. Mount a named volume on /config or a redeploy is a factory reset with the media still sitting there. Mount /metadata too (cover art, cached images, and the app's own backups). And mount /audiobooks and /podcasts, which is where the actual media goes. Four mounts, and losing any one of them loses something the others cannot rebuild."
25	  - "SET JWT_SECRET_KEY EXPLICITLY. TokenManager.js:42-56: if it is unset, a random 256-byte secret is generated ONCE and stored inside the SQLite settings, and Server.js:268-280 reuses the same value as the express-session secret. That is fine until /config is rebuilt, at which point every mobile app and browser extension holding a token is signed out and every issued API key JWT stops verifying. Generate one alphanumeric value, set it in the compose environment, and record it wherever the user keeps deploy secrets so the next redeploy reuses the same one. Never write the value into this file."
26	  - "PORT: THE CONTAINER LISTENS ON 80 AND THE PUBLISHED HOST PORT IS 13378. Dockerfile:60-63 sets ENV PORT=80 and EXPOSE 80; upstream's own compose publishes 13378:80 and its comment says to change only the external side. deploy_compose's port parameter is the HOST port, so pass 13378, not 80. Publishing on 80 would also collide with anything else the VM wants that port for. Health probe: GET /healthcheck returns 200 with an empty body, GET /status returns JSON that identifies the app."
27	  - "IT ANSWERS ON BOTH / AND /audiobookshelf, WHICH LOOKS LIKE A BUG AND IS NOT. index.js:52 defaults ROUTER_BASE_PATH to '/audiobookshelf', and Server.js:289-300 rewrites every request that does not already start with that prefix to include it. So the root URL works normally. Do not set ROUTER_BASE_PATH to fix a problem you do not have; it exists for hosting the app under a subpath of a shared domain, which is not what a redu dname is."
28	  - "LEAVE THE SSRF FILTER ALONE. Server.js:60-88: the request filter is ON by default and is turned OFF by either EXP_PROXY_SUPPORT=1 or DISABLE_SSRF_REQUEST_FILTER=1. This app fetches podcast feeds and cover images from URLs its users supply, so disabling the filter turns the instance into a probe into redu's private network, including the user's own other machines. Neither variable belongs in this deploy. If a specific host genuinely needs allowing, SSRF_REQUEST_FILTER_WHITELIST takes a comma-separated hostname list and is the narrow tool."
29	  - "THE APP'S OWN BACKUPS ARE NOT A BACKUP OF THE VM. ServerSettings.js:32,108 defaults backupPath to <METADATA_PATH>/backups, so the scheduled backups land on the same disk as the thing they are backing up. They protect against a bad edit or a failed upgrade, not against losing the machine. For that, use redu's own backup of the volume, and say which one you mean when you tell the user they are backed up."

40	# Self-host Audiobookshelf on redu
41	
42	Your own audiobook and podcast server, in the EU, on a machine you control: one Node container, a
43	public HTTPS URL, and the official Android and iOS apps talking straight to it.
44	
45	## What this deploys
46	
47	- **Audiobookshelf** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.medium VM. Port 80 in the
48	  container, published on 13378.
49	- **No database service.** The app is SQLite-only by design, so there is nothing managed to
50	  provision and nothing extra to pay for.
51	- Four volumes: `/config` (which IS the database), `/metadata`, `/audiobooks`, `/podcasts`.
52	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
53	
54	About GBP 0.028/hour, roughly GBP 20 a month. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.
55	
56	## Read this before you size it: the disk is the constraint, not the RAM
57	
58	Audiobooks are big and they live on the VM. The flavor disk is your entire storage budget:
59	
60	| Flavor | vCPU / RAM | Disk | GBP/hr | Trial |

# Self-host Audiobookshelf on redu

Your own audiobook and podcast server, in the EU, on a machine you control: one Node container, a
public HTTPS URL, and the official Android and iOS apps talking straight to it.

- **Audiobookshelf** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.medium VM. Port 80 in the
  container, published on 13378.
- **No database service.** The app is SQLite-only by design, so there is nothing managed to
  provision and nothing extra to pay for.
- Four volumes: `/config` (which IS the database), `/metadata`, `/audiobooks`, `/podcasts`.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

Audiobooks are big and they live on the VM. The flavor disk is your entire storage budget:

| Flavor | vCPU / RAM | Disk | GBP/hr | Trial |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| m1.small | 1 / 2 | **20 GB** | 0.0174 | yes |
| m1.medium | 2 / 4 | **40 GB** | 0.0278 | yes, at the ceiling |
| m1.large | 4 / 8 | **80 GB** | 0.0486 | **no** |

backups. On another redu deployment an m1.medium reported 32.4 GB free of its 40 GB after an app

Work out the size of the library first, then pick. If it is larger than the disk, the answer is a

  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /status carried neither isInit true nor false." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# 3. CLAIM IT. Alphanumeric only, so there is nothing to escape in JSON or the shell.
#    The body goes in on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on this machine.
ABS_PASS=[REDACTED:value] tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 32)
printf '{"newRoot":{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}}' "$ABS_USER" "$ABS_PASS" > "$TMP/init"
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/init" "https://$HOST/init")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: POST /init answered HTTP $code. The instance is UNCLAIMED and reachable." >&2
  echo "  Do not leave it up. Claim it by hand or delete the deployment." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 4. PROVE THE OUTCOME, NOT THE STATUS CODE. A 200 from /init is not proof the password works.
printf '{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$ABS_USER" "$ABS_PASS" > "$TMP/login"
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/me" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/login" "https://$HOST/login")
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -q '"user"' "$TMP/me"; then
  echo "FAIL: signing in as $ABS_USER returned HTTP $code and no user object." >&2
  echo "  The account may exist with a password you do not have. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: signed in as $ABS_USER, so the account exists and the password works."

# 5. THE NEGATIVE HALF, which only means something because step 4 passed. A root user created
#    with an empty password logs in with an empty password, from anywhere. Prove that cannot
#    happen here. EMPTY is a variable so no literal credential is ever written down.
EMPTY=""
for u in root "$ABS_USER"; do
  printf '{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$u" "$EMPTY" > "$TMP/empty"
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/empty" "https://$HOST/login")
  if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: the account '$u' logs in with NO PASSWORD. Fix this before anything else." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "OK: '$u' with an empty password is refused (HTTP $code)."
done

# 6. And confirm the window is now shut.
curl -sSL "https://$HOST/status" | grep -q '"isInit":true' || {
  echo "FAIL: /status still does not report isInit true. POST /init may still be open." >&2
  exit 1
}
echo
echo "CLAIMED. Root user: $ABS_USER"
echo "Password (shown once, store it now): $ABS_PASS"

# Self-host Audiobookshelf on redu

Your own audiobook and podcast server, in the EU, on a machine you control: one Node container, a
public HTTPS URL, and the official Android and iOS apps talking straight to it.

## What this deploys

- **Audiobookshelf** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.medium VM. Port 80 in the
  container, published on 13378.
- **No database service.** The app is SQLite-only by design, so there is nothing managed to
  provision and nothing extra to pay for.
- Four volumes: `/config` (which IS the database), `/metadata`, `/audiobooks`, `/podcasts`.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.028/hour, roughly GBP 20 a month. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Read this before you size it: the disk is the constraint, not the RAM

Audiobooks are big and they live on the VM. The flavor disk is your entire storage budget:

| Flavor | vCPU / RAM | Disk | GBP/hr | Trial |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| m1.small | 1 / 2 | **20 GB** | 0.0174 | yes |
| m1.medium | 2 / 4 | **40 GB** | 0.0278 | yes, at the ceiling |
| m1.large | 4 / 8 | **80 GB** | 0.0486 | **no** |

## The compose

Upstream's `docker-compose.yml` is labelled `### EXAMPLE DOCKER COMPOSE ###` and pins
`:latest`. This is the same shape with a real version, named volumes instead of host bind mounts,
and the JWT secret set explicitly:

```yaml
services:
  audiobookshelf:
    image: ghcr.io/advplyr/audiobookshelf:2.36.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      JWT_SECRET_KEY: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      TZ: "${ABS_TZ}"
    volumes:
      - abs-config:/config
      - abs-metadata:/metadata
      - abs-audiobooks:/audiobooks
      - abs-podcasts:/podcasts
    ports:
      - "13378:80"
volumes:
  abs-config:
  abs-metadata:
  abs-audiobooks:
  abs-podcasts:
```

`ABS_JWT_SECRET` is yours to generate, once, and to reuse on every redeploy. `ABS_TZ` is
cosmetic (it sets the container clock for scheduled tasks and log timestamps).

## The one that actually breaks it

**The first request wins.** There is no install wizard and no admin account created from
environment variables. `POST /init` is unauthenticated and stays open until a root user exists,
and if the caller sends an empty password the root account is created **with no password**, which
then logs in from anywhere. Between the container going healthy and you claiming the account,
whoever loads the URL owns the server.

Nothing in the configuration closes that window. The only thing that closes it is claiming the
account, which is why it is a script and not a paragraph.

The good news is on the other side of it: Audiobookshelf has **no self-signup route at all**, so
once root exists the door is shut permanently and there is no registration setting to remember.

## Claim the root account, and prove you did

Run this the moment the deploy reports ready, before the URL goes anywhere.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claim the Audiobookshelf root account and verify the claim.
#   ./claim.sh audiobookshelf-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud myusername
# Exit 0 = claimed and verified, 1 = FAILED (do not leave this instance up),
#          2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting; re-run).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: claim.sh <host> <username>}"
ABS_USER="${2:?usage: claim.sh <host> <username>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. redu's proxy answers 502 for roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts,
#    and an error page fails every assertion below in a way that reads like a pass. Require 200
#    AND require the app to identify itself, before anything else runs.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/status" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/status")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /status answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
    echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the container starts. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"app":"audiobookshelf"' "$TMP/status"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /status returned 200 but does not identify as Audiobookshelf." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: Audiobookshelf is serving on https://$HOST"

# 2. IS THE WINDOW STILL OPEN? isInit is false until a root user exists.
if grep -q '"isInit":true' "$TMP/status"; then
  echo "FAIL: a root user ALREADY EXISTS and it is not one you created." >&2
  echo "  Somebody claimed this instance first. Delete the deployment and start again;" >&2
  echo "  POST /init is one-shot and there is no way to take it back." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -q '"isInit":false' "$TMP/status"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /status carried neither isInit true nor false." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# 3. CLAIM IT. Alphanumeric only, so there is nothing to escape in JSON or the shell.
#    The body goes in on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on this machine.
ABS_PASS=[REDACTED:value] tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 32)
printf '{"newRoot":{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}}' "$ABS_USER" "$ABS_PASS" > "$TMP/init"
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/init" "https://$HOST/init")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: POST /init answered HTTP $code. The instance is UNCLAIMED and reachable." >&2
  echo "  Do not leave it up. Claim it by hand or delete the deployment." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 4. PROVE THE OUTCOME, NOT THE STATUS CODE. A 200 from /init is not proof the password works.
printf '{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$ABS_USER" "$ABS_PASS" > "$TMP/login"
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/me" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/login" "https://$HOST/login")
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -q '"user"' "$TMP/me"; then
  echo "FAIL: signing in as $ABS_USER returned HTTP $code and no user object." >&2
  echo "  The account may exist with a password you do not have. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: signed in as $ABS_USER, so the account exists and the password works."

# 5. THE NEGATIVE HALF, which only means something because step 4 passed. A root user created
#    with an empty password logs in with an empty password, from anywhere. Prove that cannot
#    happen here. EMPTY is a variable so no literal credential is ever written down.
EMPTY=""
for u in root "$ABS_USER"; do
  printf '{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$u" "$EMPTY" > "$TMP/empty"
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/empty" "https://$HOST/login")
  if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: the account '$u' logs in with NO PASSWORD. Fix this before anything else." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "OK: '$u' with an empty password is refused (HTTP $code)."
done

# 6. And confirm the window is now shut.
curl -sSL "https://$HOST/status" | grep -q '"isInit":true' || {
  echo "FAIL: /status still does not report isInit true. POST /init may still be open." >&2
  exit 1
}
echo
echo "CLAIMED. Root user: $ABS_USER"
echo "Password (shown once, store it now): $ABS_PASS"
```

## Checking the storage, once there is something in it

```bash
# On the VM, via get_ssh_command. Note redu's VMs run docker, not podman:
# a command that does not exist prints an error and greps to zero matches, which reads as a pass.
C=$(sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -i audiobookshelf | head -n1)
[ -n "$C" ] || { echo "no audiobookshelf container found; nothing below means anything" >&2; exit 1; }

# Positive half: the SQLite database is on the mounted volume, which is what /config being a
# real volume actually means.
sudo docker exec "$C" ls -l /config/absdatabase.sqlite

# Negative half: nothing large is sitting on the container's own writable layer.
sudo docker exec "$C" du -sh /audiobooks /podcasts /metadata /config

# And the number that decides whether this VM is the right size.
df -h /
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claim the Audiobookshelf root account and verify the claim.
#   ./claim.sh audiobookshelf-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud myusername
# Exit 0 = claimed and verified, 1 = FAILED (do not leave this instance up),
#          2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting; re-run).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: claim.sh <host> <username>}"
ABS_USER="${2:?usage: claim.sh <host> <username>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. redu's proxy answers 502 for roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts,
#    and an error page fails every assertion below in a way that reads like a pass. Require 200
#    AND require the app to identify itself, before anything else runs.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/status" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/status")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /status answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
    echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the container starts. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"app":"audiobookshelf"' "$TMP/status"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /status returned 200 but does not identify as Audiobookshelf." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: Audiobookshelf is serving on https://$HOST"

# 2. IS THE WINDOW STILL OPEN? isInit is false until a root user exists.
if grep -q '"isInit":true' "$TMP/status"; then
  echo "FAIL: a root user ALREADY EXISTS and it is not one you created." >&2
  echo "  Somebody claimed this instance first. Delete the deployment and start again;" >&2
  echo "  POST /init is one-shot and there is no way to take it back." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -q '"isInit":false' "$TMP/status"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /status carried neither isInit true nor false." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# 3. CLAIM IT. Alphanumeric only, so there is nothing to escape in JSON or the shell.
#    The body goes in on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on this machine.
ABS_PASS=[REDACTED:value] tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 32)
printf '{"newRoot":{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}}' "$ABS_USER" "$ABS_PASS" > "$TMP/init"
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/init" "https://$HOST/init")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: POST /init answered HTTP $code. The instance is UNCLAIMED and reachable." >&2
  echo "  Do not leave it up. Claim it by hand or delete the deployment." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 4. PROVE THE OUTCOME, NOT THE STATUS CODE. A 200 from /init is not proof the password works.
printf '{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$ABS_USER" "$ABS_PASS" > "$TMP/login"
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/me" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/login" "https://$HOST/login")
if [ "$code" != "200" ] || ! grep -q '"user"' "$TMP/me"; then
  echo "FAIL: signing in as $ABS_USER returned HTTP $code and no user object." >&2
  echo "  The account may exist with a password you do not have. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: signed in as $ABS_USER, so the account exists and the password works."

# 5. THE NEGATIVE HALF, which only means something because step 4 passed. A root user created
#    with an empty password logs in with an empty password, from anywhere. Prove that cannot
#    happen here. EMPTY is a variable so no literal credential is ever written down.
EMPTY=""
for u in root "$ABS_USER"; do
  printf '{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$u" "$EMPTY" > "$TMP/empty"
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @"$TMP/empty" "https://$HOST/login")
  if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: the account '$u' logs in with NO PASSWORD. Fix this before anything else." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "OK: '$u' with an empty password is refused (HTTP $code)."
done

# 6. And confirm the window is now shut.
curl -sSL "https://$HOST/status" | grep -q '"isInit":true' || {
  echo "FAIL: /status still does not report isInit true. POST /init may still be open." >&2
  exit 1
}
echo
echo "CLAIMED. Root user: $ABS_USER"
echo "Password (shown once, store it now): $ABS_PASS"

Deployed and claimed.

## Audiobookshelf is live

**https://audiobookshelf-jr969jvc.redu.cloud**

| | |
|---|---|
| Root user | `admin` |
| Root password | `«REDACTED:entropy:0b2c9d6f»` |
| `JWT_SECRET_KEY` | `«REDACTED:entropy:07b1000a»` |

**Store both now.** Neither is written into `redu.md` — the password is the only copy, and the JWT secret must be reused verbatim on any redeploy or every phone app and API key gets signed out. SSH: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/redu-deploy-test -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -p 22023 ubuntu@audiobookshelf-jr969jvc.redu.cloud`

**The root account was claimed before the URL existed anywhere else.** `POST /init` is unauthenticated and one-shot, so I armed the claim to fire the moment the app answered rather than waiting to notice. It went at 305s, with `isInit` still `false` — nobody got there first. Verified rather than assumed: login as `admin` succeeded, and an empty-password login was refused (HTTP 401) for both `root` and `admin`. Audiobookshelf has no self-signup route at all, so that door is now shut permanently — the only way anyone else gets an account is you creating one in Settings.

**Deployed shape** — deployment 435, VM `5b27ce48`, m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB), port 13378, **£0.0278/hr ≈ £20/mo**, inside the no-card trial. `plan_deploy` quoted m1.large at £35.48/mo because a compose stack was declared; `flavor_id "3"` held m1.medium, saving ~43%. No managed database — the app is SQLite-only, so there was nothing to provision.

**Verified on the VM, not assumed:** image `2.36.0` running with `restart=unless-stopped`; all four mounts are real named volumes (`app-src_abs-config` etc.) with the database at `/config/absdatabase.sqlite`; `JWT_SECRET_KEY` present in the container; SSRF filter left on (`EXP_PROXY_SUPPORT` and `DISABLE_SSRF_REQUEST_FILTER` both unset). Idle usage: 585 MB RAM of 3915, and **35 GB of 38 GB disk free** — the first measured numbers for this app, now written into `redu.md`.

Two things worth knowing before you load it up:

- **The disk is the ceiling and it isn't resizable.** You said under ~30 GB, and you have ~35 GB. Going past it is a block-volume create + attach + format + mount + fstab + compose bind-mount job, far easier to do before there's a library on the machine than after.
- **`delete_deployment` here is total.** No managed database survives it — the SQLite database, metadata, covers and all media are on this VM's disk. Take a volume backup first if the library matters. Also note the app's own scheduled backups land in `/metadata/backups`, i.e. the same disk they're protecting.

Files written: `redu-deploy-plan.md` (real deployed values, replacing the estimate), `docker-compose.yml`, `claim.sh`, and `redu.md` updated with the pinned dname, the deploy-log entry, and four new measured quirks — including that the claim window opens at ~5 minutes, not the 2.5 the file predicted. I hand-edited those in rather than round-tripping the file through the server merge, since that merge appends only the log line and would have dropped the new quirks.
